items.title: 2026-018: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory: two critical PHP vulnerabilities enabling unauthenticated remote code execution were fixed in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. PoCs are circulating, raising the risk of active exploitation.

items.title: 2026-019: Critical Vulnerability in GitLab Community and Enterprise Editions
items.summary: GitLab patched a critical flaw allowing unauthenticated arbitrary code execution on GitLab servers. CERT-EU urges prioritised patching of internet-facing instances and compromise assessment.

items.title: 2026-017: Critical Vulnerability in Cisco Secure Email Gateway
items.summary: Cisco Secure Email Gateway AMP feature contains a critical flaw allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to write files and run commands as root; Cisco PSIRT confirms active exploitation.

items.title: The PHP Meltdown Shows How AI Makes Bugs More Exploitable
items.summary: Wired reports AI tools helped researchers surface years-old PHP vulnerabilities, after which AI-assisted exploitation attempts quickly followed, shortening the window between disclosure and attack.

items.title: Brotli Decoder Flaw Behind Node.js RCE Also Affects Bun, Python and Other Widely Used Software
items.summary: CVE-2026-111497, a memory-corruption flaw in Google's Brotli decoder behind a Node.js RCE, also affects Bun, Python Brotli/brotlicffi packages and Envoy proxies decompressing Brotli.

items.title: BlackX UEFI bootkit exploits Baton Drop flaw to bypass Secure Boot
items.summary: A new UEFI bootkit called BlackX, used in an early-2026 espionage campaign, abuses the old Baton Drop flaw to bypass Secure Boot and load a driver that disables Kaspersky and Avast protections.

items.title: Autonomous attack agent in 'Skynet mode' hijacks other models to carry out its evil deeds
items.summary: Researchers describe an autonomous attack agent able to run up to 100,000 steps without human approval and hijack other models to execute attacks.

items.title: Leaked LiteLLM Master Key Let Attackers Steal GitHub Tokens and Hijack Release Pipeline
items.summary: LiteLLM disclosed that a master key committed to a public GitHub repo in May 2026 let an attacker steal GitHub tokens and publish a malicious version of the Python package.

items.title: CISA Flags Two Actively Exploited Critical Flaws in Collabora Online and Arista VeloCloud
items.summary: CISA added two actively exploited critical flaws to KEV: CVE-2026-110447 (CVSS 9.2) in Collabora Online CODE Server and a vulnerability in Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator.

items.title: Inside the cyber flaw scramble that brought the AI threat to life
items.summary: Politico reconstructs the 72-hour scramble by cybersecurity agencies worldwide after critical flaws were found in PHP, framing it as the moment the AI-driven threat became tangible.

items.title: Keeping pace with e-evidence: New report examines Europe’s digital forensic capabilities
items.summary: A European Commission/Europol report finds EU digital forensic tools, resources and expertise are failing to keep pace with the volume and complexity of modern e-evidence.

items.title: Bots, deepfakes and surveillance: Israel’s election goes to war online
items.summary: Israel's election campaign features heavy use of bots, deepfakes and data-driven surveillance by rival camps days before the vote.

items.title: Bulgarians vote for president in shadow of Russia’s war on Ukraine
items.summary: Bulgarians vote for president against the backdrop of Russia's war on Ukraine and recent deadly Black Sea drone strikes.

items.title: Iran has ramped up efforts to target US personnel, intelligence memo warns
items.summary: A US intelligence memo warns that Iran has intensified efforts to target US personnel, suggesting heightened state-linked threat activity.

items.title: Google Says Gmail and Photos Data Shared With AI Search Could Be Used for Targeted Ads
items.summary: Google's updated privacy policy clarifies that data from Gmail and Photos shared with AI features in Search or Gemini may be used for targeted advertising.

items.title: Starlink connection restored at high speed in Ukraine, defense minister says
items.summary: Ukraine's defence minister says Starlink connectivity has been restored at full speed after restrictions imposed the previous week.

items.title: Researchers Push Over 2 Million Updates to Remotely Disable Popcorn Time Updater That Could Fuel a Botnet
items.summary: Dutch firm Eye Security pushed over 2 million updates to third-party machines to disable an abandoned Time4Popcorn updater that could have been abused to build a botnet, raising legal and ethical questions.

items.title: Moonshot curbs hacking ability in new Kimi model as fears grow over AI-powered cyberattacks
items.summary: Moonshot has restricted hacking-related capabilities in its new Kimi model amid growing concern about AI-enabled cyberattacks.

items.title: 27 arrests and 248 potential victims identified in action week against labour exploitation
items.summary: Europol, ELA and 34 countries ran an action week against labour exploitation, leading to 27 arrests and 248 potential victims identified across agriculture, construction and hospitality sectors.

items.title: 5th EMPACT Hackathon leads to the detection of 51 potential victims
items.summary: The 5th EMPACT Hackathon in Amsterdam brought 40 investigators from 20 countries to target digital aspects of human trafficking, identifying 51 potential victims and five suspects.

items.title: Security Sunday: Bringen Frankreichs Proteste Marine Le Pen an die Macht? – mit Martina Meister
items.summary: German-language Politico podcast discussing whether escalating French protests over energy prices could benefit Marine Le Pen amid Macron's weakening position.

items.title: Serbia votes in election pitting longtime leader against student movement
items.summary: Serbia holds a tight election pitting incumbent Aleksandar Vucic against an anticorruption student movement.

items.title: Almost 1,000 arrested as clashes follow another day of mass protests across France
items.summary: Nearly 1,000 arrests followed mass protests across France, with demonstrations spreading to other European countries.

items.title: Thousands rally in Turkiye over journalist arrests, media shutdowns
items.summary: Thousands protested across Türkiye against journalist arrests and restrictions on independent media.

items.title: Serbia votes as students seek to unseat Vucic in snap election
items.summary: Serbia's snap election sees a student-led movement attempting to unseat President Vucic.

items.title: Violence breaks out across Europe after another day of protests
items.summary: Police clashed with demonstrators in France, Italy and Spain over living costs and public service cuts, indicating broad European unrest.
